name: 餅屋半兵衛 浅草 (Mochiya Hanbei Asakusa)

claims.text: No information found on cross-contamination handling; the shop is not positioned as gluten-free and mixes wheat flour directly into the mochi dough.

name: 名代 富士そば 水道橋店 (Nadai Fuji Soba Suidobashi)

claims.text: Fuji Soba's official allergen chart lists both wheat and buckwheat among the specified allergens even for the basic kake soba, and independent sources describe standard-branch noodles as roughly 40% buckwheat flour blended with 60% wheat flour.
As a standard soba-tsuyu shop, the seasoning broth is soy-sauce based; soy is listed on the company's own allergen chart for the basic kake soba.

The plain kake soba broth already contains fish (mackerel) per the company's allergen chart, indicating a bonito/fish-based dashi rather than a kombu-only vegan stock; no vegan-specific broth or substitution is documented.
The company publishes an official allergen reference chart covering its menu, offering more ingredient transparency than most fast standing-noodle shops.

name: つけ麺・らーめん 波海拉 (Namiura (Tsukemen & Ramen))

claims.text: The ramen is built on a dark soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) base with a dried-sardine aroma; standard shoyu contains wheat.
Broth is a pork-bone (tonkotsu) and seafood (gyokai/dried-fish) blended stock used for both the tsukemen dipping sauce and the ramen soup — not vegan or vegetarian.
The menu is built around shoyu (soy sauce) or shio (salt) tare as standard ramen bases; no wheat-free soy sauce or gluten-free broth preparation was mentioned in any source covering the shop.

name: 肉うどん 肉めし 甚三 渋谷本店 (Nikuudon Nikumeshi Jinza Shibuya Honten)

claims.text: Soy sauce used in the broth is sourced from Kagawa/Setouchi producers using traditional wheat-based shoyu.
The base dashi broth is made with iriko (dried anchovies), and the signature menu centers on Chiba-sourced pork (niku udon, niku meshi), so shared broths and kitchen equipment are not vegan-free.

name: 農 おおはし (Nou Ohashi (No Ohashi))

claims.text: The restaurant's own description emphasizes fresh, seasonal vegetables shipped directly from its affiliated Ohashi Farm in Gifu, forming the base of colorful salads, vegetable tempura, and other vegetable-centered dishes, which gives naturally plant-forward options on the menu even though it is not a dedicated vegan restaurant.

name: おばんざい味ゆぅ (Obanzai Miyuu (Aji-Yuu))

claims.text: The daily menu emphasizes seasonal vegetables and homemade miso, giving it a naturally plant-leaning lean-up, though this has not been documented as a formal vegan or allergy-safe program.

The shop's signature okonomiyaki sauce is a thick, Worcestershire-style sauce and the dishes are built around wheat-flour batter and wheat soba/udon noodles from Hiroshima, so wheat is a core, unavoidable ingredient rather than an optional condiment.
